vca_treats.title: Choosing Healthy Treats for Dogs & Cats
vca_treats.quote: treats should make up no more than 10% of your dog's daily caloric intake; As with dogs, cat treats shouldn't make up more than 10% of your cat's daily caloric intake, and 5% is even better.

tufts_linder_treats_2021.title: Treat Options for Dogs and Cats Without Unbalancing Their Diet
tufts_linder_treats_2021.reviewer: Deborah E. Linder, DVM, MS, DACVIM (Nutrition) (author); post date 2021-10-21
tufts_linder_treats_2021.quote: Reminder that your pet should only receive 10% of their daily calories from treats so you don't unbalance their diet!

tufts_freeman_growth_2022.title: Growth Guide: Keeping your Puppy on the Right Track
tufts_freeman_growth_2022.reviewer: Lisa M. Freeman, DVM, PhD, DACVIM (Nutrition) (author); post date 2022-01-31
tufts_freeman_growth_2022.quote: Too many calories from puppy food, treats, and other foods during growth can cause puppies to become overweight. PLEASE don't change to an adult food before 12 months of age in small, medium, or large-sized breeds (the page gives 18 months for large-breed puppies in parentheses).

tufts_linder_bland_2022.title: Does My Pet Need a 'Bland Diet'?
tufts_linder_bland_2022.reviewer: Deborah E. Linder, DVM, MS, DACVIM (Nutrition) (author); post date 2022-02-22
tufts_linder_bland_2022.quote: one low fat example is cooked white rice and cooked chicken or turkey breast in a 2:1 ratio. You'll want to remove any skin or bones and avoid any added seasoning or butter/oil. if fed long-term (weeks to months), this type of diet can cause serious harm to pets!

vca_salmon_poisoning.quote: dogs eat raw or undercooked salmon. Cats do not appear to develop salmon poisoning.

vca_tuna_cats.title: True or False: Milk and tuna are great foods for cats
vca_tuna_cats.quote: Cats of all ages should not be fed milk or tuna. While cats may love tuna, they shouldn't eat it—not even as a treat!

cornell_feeding_cat.title: Feeding Your Cat
cornell_feeding_cat.reviewer: not shown on page; page states last updated Thursday, Apr 30, 2026
cornell_feeding_cat.quote: Cats are obligate carnivores, which means that they rely on nutrients found only in animal products. A good rule of thumb is not to let treats exceed 10 to 15 percent of a cat's daily caloric intake. Some cats that have consumed canned fish products meant for humans have developed potentially serious neurological disorders.

vca_thiamine.title: Thiamine
vca_thiamine.quote: These items contain high concentrations of enzymes called thiaminases, which degrade thiamine. Cooking destroys thiaminases. (Species not named on the page; the page is a drug-information article.)
